clue.text: Stops in the theatre

definitions.meaning: a vehicle or engine that cuts out and halts
the seats on the ground floor of a theatre, in front of the stage

explanation.definitionFit: To stall is to come to a halt, and the stalls are a theatre's ground-floor seating, so one word covers both senses.

clue.text: Rose faced Irishman and refused to budge

indicators.note: the rising piece faces, so stands in front of, the Irishman

parts.note: rose, as in got to one's feet, means stood
Pat, short for Patrick, is a stock name for an Irishman

explanation.surface: A woman named Rose confronted an Irish fellow and would not move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a woman's name but is the verb rise in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand firm and not change one's position or decision.

clue.text: Skill is an essential in his job

definitions.text: Skill is an essential in his job

parts.note: art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: Craftsmanship is a must for a certain kind of worker.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a skilled craftsman while ART, IS and AN spell out the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman works with his hands, so skill matters most in such a trade.

clue.text: A man with real estate may employ him

definitions.text: A man with real estate may employ him

parts.words: A man with real estate may employ him
parts.note: a landowner hires someone to manage his property and tenants

explanation.definitionFit: A steward who manages an estate on behalf of its owner, collecting rents and overseeing farms.

clue.text: Go bananas when there's a weirdo at large

parts.note: a weirdo is a freak, an oddball
an escaped prisoner at large is out, free

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper on learning a strange person is roaming loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when there's a' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang for losing control or becoming wildly agitated.

clue.text: Devious rep got arrested. Not a good move

indicators.note: devious means winding or crooked, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A dishonest salesman was taken into custody, which was unwise.
explanation.definitionFit: A backward step, a change that makes things worse rather than better.

clue.text: Saw a dunderhead get on

parts.note: the head of the word dunder is its first letter, D
to get on is to grow older, to age

explanation.surface: Seeing a fool grow old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past of see, but it is the noun meaning a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or proverb, another word for a maxim.

clue.text: Wretched poet without time to work

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the scrambled poet goes round the time
wretched means miserable or in bad shape, so the letters are mangled

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A miserable versifier is left with no time for his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wretched' makes OPTE from POET, and 'without' puts it round ERA.
explanation.definitionFit: To function or run, as a machine does.

clue.text: Piece of soap with medicinal qualities

definitions.text: Piece of soap with medicinal qualities

parts.words: Piece of soap with medicinal qualities
parts.note: a bar of soap is called this, and so is a pill taken as medicine

explanation.definitionFit: A cake of soap is so named, and a pill is a medicinal one.

clue.text: Taking over during a siege, maybe

definitions.text: Taking over during a siege, maybe

parts.words: Taking over during a siege, maybe
parts.note: the idiom for standing in for someone, read literally as defending a stronghold under attack

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means covering for someone in their absence; literally, defending a stronghold.

clue.text: Twice dismissed for being unqualified

definitions.meaning: dismissed, as a batsman is, is 'out'; twice over gives the answer

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is read playfully: out once and then out again, joined by 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: An absolute rogue is a thorough one, utterly without qualification, which is what the phrase describes.

clue.text: A native of Belgrade sounds bitter

indicators.note: the phrase before it is spoken, and the answer is what a listener would hear

parts.note: Belgrade is the capital of Serbia, so a native of it is a Serb, giving a Serb

explanation.surface: Someone from Serbia's capital comes across as sour in tone.
explanation.definitionFit: An acerb remark is sharp and sour, a less common form of acerbic.

clue.text: Album difficult for cockney to relinquish

parts.note: a record album is a disc

indicators.note: London cockneys famously drop the H at the start of words, so the leading H goes

parts.note: difficult means hard

explanation.surface: A Londoner finds it tough to part with a favourite record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for cockney' turns HARD into 'ARD, the dropped aitch of East London speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To discard something is to throw it away or give it up.

clue.text: Intimidate old lady needing directions

parts.note: Vera is a woman's name, standing for any lady
W and E are the compass points west and east

explanation.surface: An elderly woman asks the way and frightens the person she asks.
explanation.definitionFit: To overawe is to subdue someone through fear or respect, to cow them.

clue.text: Musical girl

definitions.meaning: the stage show about the orphan Little Orphan ...

explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of a famous Broadway show and also a common female first name.

clue.text: Tapered bolt in boy's clutch

indicators.note: the bolt sits within the boy's grasp, so one piece goes inside the other
a clutch holds something within it, so the boy's name encloses the other piece

parts.note: Ned is a boy's name, short for Edward
a bolt is a short arrow fired from a crossbow

explanation.surface: A lad holds a crossbow bolt that comes to a point.
explanation.definitionFit: Something narrowed has become thinner towards one end, as a tapered object does.

clue.text: Work of art seldom produced

indicators.note: produced as in brought forth in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fine paintings are rarely created.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' joins the definition to the anagram of ART SELDOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting by a great European artist from before about 1800 is called this.

clue.text: Giant deficit accepted by fellow-American

indicators.note: the deficit is taken in by the other pieces, which go around it

parts.note: co-, as in co-worker, means fellow or joint
US stands for American, as in US forces
a deficit is a loss

explanation.surface: A huge shortfall is taken on by a partner from the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: A colossus is a huge statue, and by extension any giant figure.

clue.text: Novel a student understood

indicators.note: novel means new or fresh, so the letters are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A book a pupil grasped without difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book; it signals an anagram of A STUDENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something understood without being said is tacit, left unsaid.

clue.text: Said sister's unsurpassed all the time

indicators.note: the following words are spoken, and the answer is how they sound

parts.note: a sister is a nun, and unsurpassed means top, giving nun's top

explanation.surface: Someone claims their sibling is constantly the best.
explanation.definitionFit: Continuously, without a break or pause.

clue.text: Caused by love song for two coming first

indicators.note: the song is placed before the love, so the order in the clue is turned round

parts.note: a duet is a piece for two performers
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Romance blooms because a pair sang together first.
explanation.definitionFit: Owing to or because of: a result is attributed to its cause.

clue.text: Domains that fill EU members with fury

indicators.note: one piece is filled up, so the other goes inside
the filling material is named after with, the fury

parts.note: European MPs, E plus MPS, sit in the EU parliament
ire means fury or anger

explanation.surface: Territories that make European parliamentarians angry.
explanation.definitionFit: An empire is a realm or territory ruled by one sovereign.

clue.text: I married many a European to be protected

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a great many
une is French for a, the word a European would use

explanation.surface: A man boasts of marrying many European women and remaining safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Immune means safeguarded or shielded from infection or harm.

clue.text: Perfect time for making money

parts.note: in mint condition means perfect, as new
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Now is the ideal moment to get rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Coining or the production of coins by a mint, literally making money.

clue.text: Broadcast by a leading Irish cardinal

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word is its first, so take the start

parts.note: cardinal is a deep red colour, after the robes of cardinals

explanation.surface: A senior Irish churchman's programme went out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' looks like a churchman but stands for the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Aired means transmitted on radio or television.

clue.text: Degreaser for locks

parts.note: suggests oil remover for door locks, but the locks are hair and the cleaner is a hair wash

explanation.definitionFit: A hair wash removes grease from the locks of hair on your head.

clue.text: 10, say

definitions.meaning: 10 across means absolute or thorough, as in a complete fool

explanation.walkthrough: '10' refers back to the answer at 10 across, meaning complete or absolute.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means complete or total as an adjective and to speak as a verb.

clue.text: Noted works engender conciliatory moves

definitions.meaning: pieces of music written in notes, orchestral introductions to operas
friendly approaches made to open negotiations

explanation.walkthrough: 'engender' acts only as a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: These are orchestral openings to operas and also tentative peace approaches.

clue.text: Hasten to leave without pedestrian egghead

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the leaving word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to leave is to exit
ped is a short form of pedestrian, as in ped crossing
the head of the word egg is its first letter, E

explanation.surface: Hurry off rather than wait for a slow-walking intellectual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' puts PED inside EXIT giving EXPEDIT, then E, the head of 'egg', follows. 'egghead' looks like an intellectual but is read as egg's head.
explanation.definitionFit: To speed up a process is to hurry it along.

clue.text: Takes chances after fellow conducts body-search

indicators.note: the chance-taking piece is put after the fellow

parts.note: one who takes chances risks things

explanation.surface: A man gambles while carrying out a pat-down.
explanation.definitionFit: To frisk someone is to search them by running hands over their clothes.
